To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in Crohn's disease the epithelial barrier dysfunction is caused by a lack of antimicrobial peptides, namely Paneth-cell α- and mucosal β-defensing in the small and large bowel, respectively.
in ileal CD, Paneth-cell α-Defensins are deficient, which is independent of concurrent inflammation and cannot be found in small intestinal UC (pouchitis) and graft vs. host disease.
in Crohn's disease, the Paneth cell is the main source of α-defensins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of defensins in inflammatory bowel diseases.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of epithelial dysfunction in the small intestine and colon in inflammatory bowel diseases.
the elucidation of the pathomechanisms of the epithelial barrier dysfunction in the small intestine and colon in CD and UC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the main disease locations in CD (ileum and colon) can be linked to a distinct mechanism of epithelial barrier disruption.
in CD there is a relative deficiency of α-defensins, which is independent of inflammation and NOD2 mutation.
the epithelial barrier in Crohn's disease is disturbed by a lack of defensins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the epithelial defensin deficiencies represent an important factor for the initiation of Crohn's disease, but are not the only one.
in ileal CD, Paneth cells are deficient, which is caused by a disturbed Wnt-TCFs, while in colonic CD, β-defensins are impaired, which is caused in part by a low copy number.
the epithelial barrier in CD can be seen as a complex system, in which Paneth and other cells contribute to the antimicrobial defense.
The main takeaway from our work is that
defensin deficiency is a key factor in Crohn's disease pathogenesis and that this deficiency is a consequence of disturbed Paneth-cell and mucosal differentiation.

there is a distinct barrier dysfunction in the small intestine and colon in Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, respectively, and that this can be used as a diagnostic tool to distinguish these entities.
defensins are important in maintaining the intestinal barrier and that their deficiency is an early event in the pathogenesis and maintenance of CD.
